items.title: Fourth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Search teams have recovered 1010 bodies and rescued more than 11,800 people, while around 4,000 remain unaccounted for after seven days. Over 21,000 security personnel are still working across the affected areas.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Fourth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Fifth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Floods
items.summary: Rescue teams from India, China, and South Korea are working with Nepali forces to clear tunnels and process DNA samples. About 2,500 of the estimated 3,000 people on the Mount Kailash route have returned, while around 3,900 remain missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Fifth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Floods

items.title: Diplomatic Briefing by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr Shisir Khanal on the Bhote Koshi Floods
items.summary: A flood hit the Bhote Koshi river early on 26 August and swept through Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and Chitwan. So far 1,204 bodies have been recovered, around 4,200 people remain missing and nearly 12,000 have been rescued.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Diplomatic Briefing by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr Shisir Khanal on the Bhote Koshi Floods

items.title: Sixth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Floods
items.summary: Search teams have recovered 1,252 bodies, with around 4,200 people still missing and nearly 12,000 rescued. Teams from India, China, Singapore and South Korea are helping Nepali forces with the ongoing search and tunnel work.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Sixth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Floods

items.title: Foreign nationals — missing, rescued, or contacted (NDRRMA, 1 Sep)
items.summary: Information on foreign nationals after the Bhote Koshi flood in Rasuwa is on the Department of Tourism list. The latest situation update is dated August 30.
items.citation: NDRRMA Nepal — X post (1 September 2026)

items.title: Embassy of India — identification of mortal remains (1 Sep 2026)
items.summary: Families can check photos and descriptions of remains on the Nepal Police disaster portal. Relatives needing DNA matching or handover details can email the police or contact the embassy WhatsApp helplines.
items.citation: Embassy of India, Kathmandu — Press Release (1 September 2026)

items.title: Press Briefing by the Spokesperson on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Rescue teams have brought out more than 10,000 people so far, including over 300 foreign nationals. Around 4,200 people are still unaccounted for, with 903 bodies recovered and nearly 600 foreigners from 39 countries still missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing by the Spokesperson on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Nepal Police — DNA profiling for unidentified remains
items.summary: Families of people missing in the Rasuwa and Bhote Koshi floods can help identify recovered bodies by providing DNA samples. First-degree relatives in Nepal can give a fresh blood sample and two passport photos at the Nepal Police Hospital lab in Maharajgunj or their nearest district police office.
items.citation: Nepal Police HQ — Information on DNA Profiling for unidentified Dead Bodies (31 Aug)

items.title: NDRRMA — Bhotekoshi water level rising again (31 Aug)
items.summary: The water in the Bhotekoshi River is rising again. People in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan and nearby areas should stay careful.
items.citation: NDRRMA Nepal — public warning via official channels

items.title: Press Briefing Note by Foreign Secretary on Bhote Koshi Flood (Sunday, 2:00 PM, 30 August 2026)
items.summary: After the Bhote Koshi floods, 734 bodies have been recovered and more than 8,000 people rescued so far. About 2,500 remain unaccounted for, with search and relief work still underway in the affected districts.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing Note by Foreign Secretary on Bhote Koshi Flood (Sunday, 2:00 PM, 30 August 2026)

items.title: Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Flash floods hit the Bhote Koshi River on August 26, and so far 626 bodies have been recovered while about 2400 people remain unaccounted for. Rescue teams have brought out over 4450 people, including more than 187 foreigners, from the affected districts.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.summary: Flash floods hit Nepal's Bhote Koshi River area on 26 August. So far 538 bodies have been recovered, with 511 people from 33 countries still missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026

items.title: FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang
items.summary: Rescue teams and helicopters are working at the mudslide site in Gyirong after it struck Wednesday morning. As of Thursday morning three people have been killed and 558 remain missing.
items.citation: Xinhua (Gyirong / Tibet side) — FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang
